newsitem.title: UK: GIO Australia chief plays down profits - paper.
newsitem.headline: GIO Australia chief plays down profits - paper.

text.p: GIO Australia chief Bill Jocelyn has denied speculation he will stand down this year as well as talking down market forecasts that the insurer's profits will get a boost from increased premiums, according to the Sydney Morning Herald.
The newspaper reported on Tuesday that the general insurer's shares had risen from a low of $3.17 to $3.38, closing at $3.31 on Friday.

Nevertheless, some analysts are taking a favourable view, the newspaper said. In December the average of analysts' net profit estimates for 1996-97 was $150 million versus last year's $142 million. Revisions since have lifted the average and seen some analysts tip a profit of up to $170 million.
But Mr Jocelyn is not as optimistic, arguing it will take a long time for higher premiums to flow through.
"We've had problems with the personal (insurance) lines side of things - we haven't generated as much money as people think we should.
"Frank (Robertson) has been working on it and there's been some recognition of that but I'm not confident it will appear before the first half of next year."
Mr Jocelyn also played down analysts' suggestion that GIO could use $250 million in excess capital to buy back its shares or pay a special dividend," the newspaper reported.
